notes: CBER HCT/P (reproductive-tissue bank) letter citing donor-eligibility screening/testing/recordkeeping failures under 21 CFR Part 1271 Subpart C (incomplete communicable-disease screening questionnaire, donors incorrectly determined eligible, eligibility determined before test results returned, incomplete summaries of records). No CGMP (210/211/111/820), adulteration, misbranding, or unapproved-new-drug charge is made -- the violations are all Part 1271 donor-eligibility provisions outside the given category list -- so violation_categories is left empty. Organisms field omits the communicable-disease agents named in the donor-screening questionnaire (e.g., Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhea, hepatitis, HIV, WNV) since these are disease-testing-panel references, not environmental/product-contamination organisms. recall_concern is true because FDA repeatedly directs the firm to keep non-compliant donors' HCT/Ps (oocytes, semen, embryos) in quarantine under 21 CFR 1271.60(a).
